channel.title: Mercury Bay Informer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Mercury Bay Informer (theinformer.co.nz)

item.title: Many Winners at Hunting & Fishing Junior Tournament Prize-Giving - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: Last week, Levi and Hunter Nicholson were featured in The Informer for their impressive catches in the Hunting and Fishing Junior Tournament and Youth Nationals Competition.

item.title: Romantic Comedy To See — You & Me & Tuscany - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: From the producer of Girls Trip and Ride Along, Will Packer presents a delightful romantic comedy about one little lie, one large Italian villa, and two people finding love in the most unexpected places.

item.title: Anzac Parades And Services - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: From dawn services at Fire Stations, beaches, and cemeteries to civic parades and services, there's something for everyone.

item.title: Satu — Year of the Rabbit (2024) - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: A stunning debut feature from Welsh director Joshua Trigg, this road movie captivates with its authentic performances, breathtaking cinematography, and poignant exploration of family, belonging, and the journey to find oneself.

item.title: Anzac – More Reverence And Meaning - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: This year's Anzac Day parades and services across the Peninsula saw an increase in participation, particularly from young people. The events featured open references to Christian faith and its role in remembering the loss of young life, honoring the fallen, and finding meaning beyond that to ensure freedom and peace.

item.title: Op-Shops – Not A Skip Bin In Disguise - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: In this article, we discuss the importance of responsible donations to op shops and the impact that improper disposal has on these charitable organizations.

item.title: Elected Members’ Accountability - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: Flemming Rasmussen, a local businessman and lawyer, discusses the accountability of elected members in the Mercury Bay Ward District Council.

item.title: On the Whale Trail - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: In this article, we delve into the story of a large Sperm Whale carcass that was found washed up at Matapaua in late 2022.

item.title: Theft at Small Gauge Railway - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: In this article, we report on the theft of roughly $10,000 worth of batteries from the storage of the Thames Small Gauge Railway during the night last Saturday.

item.title: Four Savvy Swaps For An Authentic Experience - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: These swaps will help you capture stunning photos, enjoy local favourites, and truly immerse yourself in the beauty of the Blue Mountains.

item.title: Are Resident And Ratepayer Associations Needed? - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: In this article, Tony Fox discusses the importance of RRAs in local democracy. They sit between us as individual citizens and the formal structures of local government, providing a collective voice that is closer to the ground than a council member or chamber, but more organized than individual complaints or submissions.

item.title: Lord Tweedsmuir Rugby Visit - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: The boys enjoyed a warm cultural welcome with Matua Marcus’s class and a haka performance. The game held last Wednesday, 18 March, was well supported by the local community, with Mercury Bay holding the lead throughout.

item.title: Beach Hop 2026 - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: Repco Beach Hop 2026 was a resounding success celebrating the best of '50s and '60s culture, from classic cars to Rock 'n' Roll music.

item.title: Go For It - As Big As You Can Grow Them - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: Hannah Hardy, the coordinator for the event, expressed her gratitude to the Placemakers Garden Centre team for their preparation and efforts in making the day successful.

item.title: Have A Good Easter - The Coromandel Informer
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, President Trump has reportedly expressed interest in purchasing New Zealand due to its volcanic lands rich in rare earth minerals.
